title: PAC-Bayesian Reinforcement Learning Trains Generalizable Policies
claim: A learning loop alternates standard training with periodic posterior updates, bound computation and adaptation, so guarantees guide exploration.
layout: Single panel, cyclic flow around central distribution plot, numbered steps with labeled arrows
description: A single-panel flow diagram with three rounded pill-shaped nodes: 'Actor (Posterior mean)' at top center, 'Critic (Posterior-aware)' at right, and 'Compute the bound' at left. Four numbered arrows connect them. Step 1 is a double-lined feedback loop between actor and critic labeled 'Normal SAC feedback loop'. Step 2, 'Periodic posterior update (every 20k environment steps)', points down from the actor to the center. There, overlapping Gaussian curves sit on an axis labeled 'Actor network parameter space'. The blue posterior is narrower and taller, and the red prior is broader and shifted right. Each has a dashed vertical mean line. Step 3 runs along the bottom axis to the left node ('Compute bound, after posterior update'). Step 4 runs to the right node ('Critic adaptation, frozen actor'). The blue and red curves draw the eye first.
caption: High-level illustration of our algorithm (PB-SAC) flow described in Section [ref], showing the interaction between the actor, critic, and bound computation components. The periodic posterior update (step 2) guides exploration through PAC-Bayes bounds (step 3) while maintaining standard Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) training (step 1) using an adaptive sampling (step 4).
abstract: We derive a novel PAC-Bayesian generalization bound for reinforcement learning that explicitly accounts for Markov dependencies in the data, through the chain's mixing time. This contributes to overcoming challenges in obtaining generalization guarantees for reinforcement learning, where the sequential nature of data breaks the independence assumptions underlying classical bounds. The new bound provides non-vacuous certificates for modern off-policy algorithms such as Soft Actor-Critic. We demonstrate the practical utility of the bound through PB-SAC, a novel algorithm that optimizes the bound during training to guide exploration. Experiments across several continuous control tasks show that the proposed approach provides meaningful confidence certificates while maintaining competitive performance.
